name: Ningera
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Gerstner-Link, Claudia. 2023. Multilateral lexical transfer among four Papuan language families: Border, Nimboran, Sentani, and Sko. In Klamer & Moro (eds.), Traces of Contact in the Lexicon, 263-306. Leiden: Brill (OA).
sources.note: Table 8.1 p.265 lists Ningera in the Bewani branch with no published source; no Ningera forms or prosody.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. Newguineaworld: Poal River (Bewani Range) page, Wayback capture 2016-09-09.
sources.note: Subpages Ainbai, Mbo, Pagi only; no Ningera page was ever archived; live site now behind Google login.

sources.citation: Rosetta Project. 2010. Ningera Swadesh List (archive.org item rosettaproject_nby_swadesh-1).
sources.note: A single entry ('cassowary: biyep'); nothing else.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark & Melissa Crowther. 2005. Meeting in the middle: interaction in North-Central New Guinea. In Pawley, Attenborough, Golson & Hide (eds.), Papuan Pasts, 167-184. Pacific Linguistics 572. Canberra: ANU. (whole volume PDF, hdl 1885/146735)
sources.note: Tables 2-4 (pp.180-182) give Ningera consonant/vowel/suprasegmental inventories from Donohue's fieldwork; p.181: 'Tonal systems are consistently absent in... the western languages (Sentani, Tobati, Ningera)'; Table 4: no pitch contrasts, contrastive nasalisation only. Nothing on where stress falls.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark & Lila San Roque. 2004. I'saka: a sketch grammar of a language of north-central New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics 554. Canberra: ANU. (hdl 1885/146726)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online
sources.note: Ningera mentioned only as a neighbouring group/language (pp. 6, 8, 14); no Ningera prosody.

sources.citation: Gerstner-Link, Claudia. 2026. Clans, spirits, land and food: Kilmeri texts. Open Text Collections 7. Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.note: Ninggera appears only as a village/biographical reference (speaker's father from Ninggera; village Yar = Ninggera); no Ningera language data.

sources.citation: OLAC resources for Ningera [nby], Wayback capture Dec 2024.
sources.note: Lists only Rosetta Swadesh list, Glottolog, Laycock Notebooks D4 (PARADISEC DL2-015) and D11 (DL2-022), Ethnologue, LINGUIST List; no language description exists in OLAC.

sources.citation: Honeyman, Thomas. 2017. A grammar of Momu, a language of Papua New Guinea. PhD thesis, ANU.
sources.note: p.41: bilabial trills areally common, 'occurring in Bewani, Mbu, Sumararu, Rawo and Ningera (Donohue et al., 2013)' [World Phonotactics Database]; nothing on Ningera stress.

sources.citation: Lewis, Simons & Fennig (eds.). 2015. Ethnologue 18th ed., Ningera [nby] (Wayback capture).
sources.note: Population 150 (2003 SIL), Border/Bewani, location; no linguistic description.

sources.citation: Ross, Bill & Mark Donohue. 2011. The many origins of diversity and complexity in phonology. Linguistic Typology 15(2) (De Gruyter first proofs, ANU open repository hdl 1885/59150).
sources.note: ex. (2c) p.259: Ningera consonant inventory 'own fieldnotes' (p k b d m n l w j plus bilabial trill series B, Bw, mB, mBw); nothing on stress or tone.

sources.citation: Brown, Robert. 1981. A sociolinguistic survey of Pagi and Kilmeri. In Loving (ed.), Sociolinguistic surveys of Sepik languages, 193-206. Workpapers in PNG Languages 29. Ukarumpa: SIL.
sources.note: p.194: 'A Ningera speaker has started work on his language under the auspices of the P.N.G. Bible Translation Association'; Ningera otherwise only located on the map. No data.

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU. (hdl 1885/146478)
sources.note: Entry 182 Ninggera (p.48, PDF p.52): 'Village: Ningera. Comments: Test DCL70 (Esi/Ningera); no other data.' Classification only.

sources.citation: Gerstner-Link, Claudia. 2018. A Grammar of Kilmeri. Pacific Linguistics 654. Berlin/Boston: De Gruyter Mouton. Ch. 1 (language setting, neighbouring Bewani languages) and sec. 2.3 'Stress' pp.73-75.

sources.note: Closest described sister language (Bewani branch); the introduction discusses Ningera as a neighbour and may contain comparative remarks; its Kilmeri stress section is the best proxy for the branch.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark, Rebecca Hetherington, James McElvenny & Virginia Dawson. 2013. World Phonotactics Database. Canberra: Department of Linguistics, ANU. Entry: Ningera.

sources.note: Database entry built from Donohue's fieldnotes; may have coded stress/tone fields for Ningera. Site offline; check Wayback (phonotactics.anu.edu.au) from a box that can reach the CDX API.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. c. 1998-2004. Ningera fieldnotes (unpublished; source of the Ningera inventories in Donohue & Crowther 2005, Ross & Donohue 2011 and the World Phonotactics Database entry).

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. n.d. Notebook D4 (Ninggera, Pagei, Rawo) and Notebook D11 (Wutung, Vanimo, Ninggera). PARADISEC collection DL2, items 015 and 022 (field wordlists, 1970).
